description: TD-PREFIX-TIDY-COLD-SPILL: age idle prefix holders' cold KV out to disk (the SECOND tiering hop: VRAM -> pinned cold pool -> spill directory). Orchestrator-side POLICY (which holder, when: age + hit history, background/idle only); the engine executes the byte moves through the KV-tiering manager. The spill directory is a CACHE, never a store: stale files are reclaimed at startup and nothing in it is load-bearing across boots.

enabled.description: Spill idle hibernated prefix holders to disk. DEFAULT TRUE (user directive 2026-08-27). Inert on architectures without a KV-tiering manager (V4) and when the path is unwritable (the feature disables LOUDLY at boot rather than failing requests).

path.description: Spill directory ('~' is expanded explicitly; created on demand). If it cannot be created or written the feature DISABLES for the boot with a loud warning — requests are never failed over spill I/O. All ls-spill-*.kvspill files in it are deleted at orchestrator startup (stale-file reclamation: a spill file is only meaningful to the engine boot that wrote it).

max_mib.description: MANDATORY byte cap over the live spill files in MiB, enforced BEFORE each write (engine-side, exact): a spill that would exceed it is refused, the orchestrator evicts the LRU SPILLED holder (deleting its file — the eviction policy over the spill directory itself) and retries once. A single 25k-token GLM holder is ~600 MiB/rank of cold KV, so an uncapped default-ON disk feature could fill a home partition. Default 32768 MiB (32 GiB).

idle_seconds.description: A hibernated holder becomes a spill candidate only after this many seconds without a hit (age + hit history, never size alone). The sweep runs only while the request queue is idle (background — never on the request path) and spills at most one holder per pass, LRU-first.
